name: Coolant Flush & Fill
primaryScope: PRIMARY found for: (a) owner manual text (US 2010 328i sedan, part no. 01 41 2 603 048, read through a third-party text mirror): cold-engine rule, cap release, 50/50 mix, MIN/MAX level check, and that the Capacities table has no coolant volume; (b) OE parts catalog (RealOEM, type code PH73 USA, selection 09/2009): expansion tank 17137640514, vent screw 11537793373, cap 17117639020, electric pump 11517586925, thermostat 11537549476, two radiator drain plugs 17117530902, no engine-block coolant drain listed; (c) BMW AG technical training documents (archive.org BMWTechnicalTrainingDocuments, ST055 Cooling Systems and ST501 Engine Mechanical): N52 electric coolant pump (200 W, 7000 l/h), N54 coolant circuit structure is the same as the N52, and the electric-pump bleed routine (heating max, blower lowest, accelerator fully down at least 10 s, engine NOT started, about 12 min, then top up to the MAX mark; to repeat, key out about 3 min), plus a warning that the pump must not run dry. The training text describes the N54 routine; applicability to the N52 rests on BMW stating the circuits are the same plus E90 N52 secondary sources. NO primary (TIS/Bentley) found for: system capacity, coolant spec code, any torque.
summary: Closed since pass 1: (1) N52 has an electric coolant pump (BMW training doc ST501/ST055, OE catalog 11517586925, Turner kit) so the automatic venting routine applies; the routine now has a PRIMARY (BMW training document, N54 text, same circuit as N52) and agrees with 5 independent non-BMW sources including the E90-specific Pelican article and two E90/E92 bimmerpost threads. (2) Post-venting top-up target: the BMW training document says top up to the MAX mark; Pelican and the 5series flush thread also say MAX; the two E60 PDFs (100 ml / 250 ml above MAX) and the E90/E92 bimmerpost ball-indicator figure (6 mm) are outlier non-BMW values, recorded as dissent. Guide uses MAX. (3) Expansion-tank bleeder (vent) screw exists: OE catalog M10 screw 11537793373, plus Pelican and bimmerpost. (4) Radiator has TWO drain plugs, qty 2, part 17117530902 (OE catalog), consistent with Pelican. (5) Engine-block drain: none on the N52 (Pelican staff, z4-forum, two 5series threads, OE catalog engine-block diagram lists no coolant drain; two dissenting posts outweighed); no block drain step. (6) 50/50 mix, cold-engine and cap-release rules now have a PRIMARY (owner manual). (7) Cap 17117639020 confirmed by OE catalog. Still unresolved: total capacity is a CONFLICT (range 7.5-8.9 L across six non-BMW figures; owner manual Capacities table lists no coolant volume; BMW training docs give none), so the guide fills by level; BMW coolant spec code is SINGLE_SOURCE (BimmerWorld Fuchs page: GS 94000 / N 600 69.0); no torque for the plastic drain plugs. Pass 4 (remote only): coolant spec code upgraded to VERIFIED_SECONDARY (second host motordoctor.fr; 'HT-12' recorded as a brand label, not a BMW code); radiator plug part and location corroborated by Pelican and bimmerpost; transmission treated as probably automatic with no effect on the procedure (fill by level, budget about 9 L); ATF is a separate system outside this guide. Capacity, expansion tank side and undertray head sizes remain open; ownerInputsNeeded is empty because the guide's branching text and fill-by-level rule cover them. Usable as an UNCERTIFIED draft.
variantDependencies: Electric coolant pump: confirmed for the N52 by BMW training documents (ST501: 200 W, 7000 l/h; ST055: N54 circuit same as N52), by OE catalog item 11517586925 for this catalog selection (E90 LCI 328i, engine N52N, block N52B30A), and by the Turner N52 pump kit. Pelican commenters report some E90s with a mechanical pump and no electric bleed cycle; those are other engines (e.g. N54) and do not apply to an N52.

Engine: RealOEM VIN page shows engine N52N and production month 09/2009 (the page does not say whether the month is decoded from the VIN or a default selection). N51 SULEV cooling layout not researched.
Radiator drain plug count: OE catalog lists 2 drain plugs (qty 2); Pelican says some E90 models have two, left and right.

Transmission: AUTOMATIC is indicated for this VIN. One free decoder (bimmer.work, run 2026-10-10 and recorded in guide 15) lists option S205 (automatic) and the RealOEM catalog row for the 3.73 final drive is tied to S205A. Still decoder-level, so 'probable'. Effect on this job: only the radiator and pipe variant (catalog lists 17117562079 for S205A/S2TBA automatic vs 17117559273 for manual) and the capacity row (Pelican about 8.2 L automatic vs 8.4 L manual; other sources reverse the direction). Neither changes the procedure: the guide fills by level and tells the reader to budget about 9 L, and the radiator cover/drain steps are the same.

Automatic transmission fluid is a separate system and is NOT part of this coolant job. The 328i N52 automatic may be a GM-built GA6L45R (BimmerWorld, ECS fitment: used from 9/2008) or a ZF GA6HP19Z (ECS lists both for the E90 328i N52); which one is in this VIN was not proven. Nothing in the coolant flush opens the transmission, and the transmission has no drain in this guide's scope; see guide 15 for the separate-system note.

Drive type: the catalog selection for model 328i shows no front differential or transfer case groups (RealOEM front axle and drive shaft groups), indicating RWD; the NHTSA decode and bimmer.work agree on a 328i (not xi). No source differentiates the cooling drain procedure by drive type.
Hot-system rule applies unchanged: cap off only when cold; the owner manual (primary) says never add coolant when the engine is hot.

tools.item: Drain pan(s), combined capacity comfortably above 9 L (about 2.5 gal); a 5-gallon bucket is what Pelican and an E60 PDF use
tools.note: Sizing derived from capacity range 7.5-8.9 L.

tools.item: Floor jack and jack stands, ramps or lift to raise and support the front so the engine undertray and radiator cover can be removed
tools.note: Pelican: lift and support the front. No source gives E90 jack points; use the owner manual jacking points.

tools.item: Undertray fastener driver: head size/type not stated by any source
tools.note: OE catalog lists the shield set as hex-head self-tapping screws ST4.8x16 (32), M6/M8 hex bolts (8), expanding nuts (14), expanding rivets (7), one rotary quick-release; it does not state head sizes. Pelican lists 13 mm sockets ("could vary"), a 6 mm Allen bit, flat and Phillips screwdrivers for the job.

tools.item: Battery charger/maintainer or regulated power supply connected at the under-hood jump-start posts (not the trunk posts)
tools.note: Dissent on equipment: a Pelican staff comment advises a vehicle power supply rather than a charger on modern cars; a z4-forum poster recommends a supply able to deliver 25 A at 14.5 V while another ran the cycles on battery alone. Pump runs about 12 minutes per cycle.

tools.item: Funnel (or transmission filler hose to see level) and distilled water
Antifreeze hydrometer or refractometer to check the mix (optional)
tools.note: Both threads suggest testing the mix.

tools.item: Rag over the expansion tank cap when first releasing pressure
Hose clamp pliers for the thermostat-side hose if used as a second drain point
tools.note: Pelican only says loosen the clamp; clamp types listed by the OE catalog are L42-48, L23-35 and L18-24 hose clamps but the thermostat-hose clamp is not tied to a type. Optional tool: only needed for the optional second drain point (step 6); the flush works without it.

parts.item: BMW coolant/antifreeze concentrate, blue (G48 formula), 1 US gal
parts.note: Three retailers (Turner, FCP Euro, BimmerWorld) list it for E90/E91/E92/E93; not an OE-catalog row (the catalog group for auxiliary fluids lists only paint). Retailers say not recommended for cars built after 2018.
Turner and FCP list it; same retailer family pattern as the gallon.
Owner manual primary: coolant is half water, half additive.
OE catalog for this selection lists 17117639020. 17117639021 (ECS/Turner) is listed for the E90 M3 only; do not use without a VIN check.
OE catalog item 02 on the expansion tank diagram. Turner/ECS part 003530ECS01A is described as replacing 17111712788 with cross-reference 11537793373.

OE catalog row 03, qty 2, number 17117530902 (catalog is the only source for the number). Existence and location corroborated by Pelican (some E90s have a left and a right plug) and a bimmerpost 2010 E90 post (plastic plug on the right side of the radiator underneath, described as a blue plastic screw, handle gently because it can become brittle).

parts.item: Electric coolant pump (only if replacing; not part of a flush; must not run dry, fill system first and store a removed pump filled with coolant per BMW training)
Thermostat (only if replacing; not part of a flush)
Hose, thermostat-to-coolant pump (replace if disturbed and brittle)
Hose clamps for the thermostat/water-pump hose group
parts.note: Which clamp sits on the hose used as a drain point is not stated.

fluids.spec: BMW coolant mixed 1:1 with distilled water. Owner manual (primary): "Coolant consists of half water and half additive"; use only suitable additives, the BMW center can recommend products.

BMW coolant spec GS 94000 / N 600 69.0 (blue, mono-ethylene-glycol, nitrite/phosphate-free, G48-type). Host 1: BimmerWorld Fuchs and genuine-BMW pages (GS 94000, N 600 690, G48). Host 2: motordoctor.fr fitment listing for the N52B30A engine (X5 E70 xDrive30i, same engine, other chassis) naming BMW N 600 69.0 (Kroon SP 11) and BMW GS 94000 (Liqui Moly KFS 11) as the manufacturer specification of antifreezes sold for that engine. 'HT-12' is a Valvoline product-range name on the same listing, not a BMW specification code; do not buy by that name. No BMW document names the code for this VIN, so the guide still says: use genuine BMW blue coolant, or a product that states GS 94000 / N 600 69.0.
fluids.note: Upgraded from SINGLE_SOURCE: second host is an engine-level fitment listing for a different chassis (same N52B30A engine), so VERIFIED_SECONDARY, primary:false. BimmerWorld's two pages remain one host.

fluids.item: Total system capacity (drain-and-refill volume is less because residue stays in the block)
fluids.spec: No BMW capacity found. Owner manual (primary) Capacities table on p. 248 lists fuel and washer fluid but NO coolant volume; page 222 gives only the level procedure.
fluids.capacity: Pelican (E90 article): about 8.2 L automatic, about 8.4 L manual. Rick (aggregate, no source named): 8.6 qt manual / 8.9 qt automatic = about 8.1 / 8.4 L. z4-forum thread: UK handbook p.103 "8.3 L" manual, a USA 3.0si manual "7.6 manual / 8.4 auto" (vehicle not clear), a TIS snippet "8 L manual with A/C", poster own 8.2 L. bimmerpost 2009 328i auto owner: just under 2 gal (about 7.5 L). Turner and Fuchs/BimmerWorld both say "8 or more liters". E60 PDF 10 L (different chassis, excluded). Working range for planning only: about 7.5 to 8.9 L; budget about 9 L of mix. Pass 4 re-check: bimmerpost (E90/E92 thread) gives 8.4 L from the Bentley manual, but for an N55 with automatic (335xi), so it is excluded for the N52. No new N52 figure found on any source; the CONFLICT stands. If the car is automatic (probable, see variantDependencies), the two sources that name automatic for a 3.0 N52 say about 8.2 L (Pelican) and about 8.4 L (z4-forum UK/US-handbook quote); fill by level and budget about 9 L.
fluids.note: Direction of the manual/automatic difference conflicts between sources, so do not infer it. Guide fills by level, not by volume.

fluids.spec: One thread used about 15 L of distilled water for three rinse/bleed cycles.

fluids.item: Hot-system safety and expansion tank cap (reference)
fluids.spec: Open the expansion tank cap only on a cold engine; turn it slightly counter-clockwise first to release pressure (BMW owner manual, primary). Pelican: 'Be sure engine has cooled before removing cap' and confirm the system lacks pressure before opening.
fluids.note: Already reflected in steps 1 and 4; listed here so the safety rule sits with the fluid rows.

torque.value: No torque value found. Two sources say tighten by hand only because the plug is plastic.
torque.note: 5series flush thread: red thumb-wheel plug, "just torque by hand if you can, since it is a piece of plastic"; E60 PDF calls it a drain plug (peacock). Qualitative only. Downgraded at merge: both URLs are on one host (5series.net thread plus its attachment).

torque.value: None on the N52 for this build
torque.conflicts: Dissent: the 2006 E60 PDF author and one zhpmafia poster describe a block drain plug (right side near cylinder 2); the same E60 author later says there is no need to remove it, and Pelican staff, a z4-forum poster ("No block drain plug on an N52"), two 5series.net threads (one citing the Bentley manual contents) and the OE catalog engine block diagram (no coolant drain listed; only M14/M16/M22 oil-system screw plugs) say there is none. Guide must not include a block drain step.

torque.value: Close until it clicks (owner manual); sources also mention aligning the arrow marks on cap and tank
No torque found; close it fully before the venting cycle
torque.note: Screw exists (3 sources) but no torque exists in any source.

torque.value: No torque or head size found

steps.title: Prepare on a cold engine and level ground
steps.instruction: Park on level ground with the engine fully cooled (ambient temperature). Do not open the cooling system warm; coolant under pressure can scald. Gather the drain pans, coolant, distilled water and stands.
warnings: Hot coolant escapes under pressure and can cause burns (owner manual: never add coolant while the engine is hot).
Coolant is toxic and attractive to animals; clean every spill.

steps.title: Connect battery support
steps.instruction: Attach a charger/maintainer, or preferably a regulated power supply, to the under-hood jump-start posts before any venting. Do not use the trunk posts. Keep it connected until the last venting cycle ends.
warnings: One bimmerpost poster warns that jumping from the trunk posts can damage the junction box.
A Pelican staff comment prefers a power supply to a charger on modern cars; voltage must stay stable for the roughly 12 minute pump cycle.

steps.title: Raise and support the front; remove the undertray and radiator cover
steps.instruction: Lift and support the front securely. Remove the engine splash shield (one E60 N52 PDF counts 8 screws; an E92 poster describes about 16 small bolts plus a metal plate with 5 bolts). Then remove the radiator cover fasteners and metal brackets (note their positions), push the cover toward the front to free its tabs from the subframe, and pull it down and out.
warnings: Never work under a car held only by a jack.
Screw count and head size on THIS car are not documented; the OE catalog shows a mixed set (self-tapping hex-head screws, M6/M8 bolts, expanding nuts and rivets).

steps.title: Release pressure and open the expansion tank cap
steps.instruction: With a rag over the cap, turn it slightly counter-clockwise to release any pressure, then continue turning to open it.
warnings: Only on a cold engine.

steps.title: Drain at the radiator
steps.instruction: Place a large pan under the left side of the radiator. Unscrew the left radiator drain plug by hand (plastic thumb-wheel; a small flat blade can help) and let it drain; refit it once the flow slows. Some E90s have a second plug on the right side: drain it the same way. Expect only about 65-70 percent of the system to come out (about 1.3-1.5 US gal reported).
warnings: The plugs are plastic; do not over-tighten or use tools to force them.
OE catalog lists two plugs (qty 2); Pelican says some models have one.

steps.title: Drain the thermostat-side hose (optional second drain point)
steps.instruction: To remove more coolant, place a pan under the right side of the car behind the sway bar, loosen the clamp on the hose at the back of the thermostat housing, pull the hose off and let it drain. Refit the hose and clamp (replace the clamp or hose if its condition is doubtful).
warnings: Location behind the sway bar is from one source (Pelican); a second poster only says to detach the lower hose at the thermostat housing.

steps.title: Do not look for a block drain
steps.instruction: The N52 has no engine block drain plug. Remove the remaining coolant by distilled-water rinse and venting cycles instead.
warnings: If a different engine code is found on the car, re-check; older E60 PDF text mentions a block plug.

steps.title: Optional distilled-water rinse
steps.instruction: Close the drains, fill with distilled water, run the automatic venting routine (step 11), drain again, and repeat until the drain runs clear. Posters used two to three rinses.
warnings: Every rinse needs its own venting cycle and a connected battery supply.

steps.title: Close the drains and refit hoses
steps.instruction: Refit the radiator drain plugs by hand, make sure the thermostat hose and clamp are seated, and check that the bleeder screw on the expansion tank is closed.
warnings: Finger-tight only on the plastic plugs.

steps.title: Mix and fill
steps.instruction: Mix BMW blue coolant 1:1 with distilled water (plan about 9 L total, capacity is uncertain). Fill the expansion tank slowly to MAX. Per Pelican and an E60 PDF, loosen the tank bleeder screw during filling until coolant comes out, then close it; an E60 venting PDF instead says fill to the lower edge of the filler neck with the cap closed during venting. Do not overfill above MAX.
warnings: Fill level before venting differs between sources (MAX per Pelican; lower edge of filler neck per an E60 PDF); the final level is set after venting in step 12.
Use only suitable coolant: owner manual warns other additives can damage the engine.

steps.title: Run the automatic venting routine
steps.instruction: Close the cap and the bleeder screw. Switch the ignition on without starting the engine. Set the heater to maximum temperature (AUTO) and the fan to its lowest setting. Press the accelerator fully to the floor and hold it for about 10 seconds, then release; the electric pump cycles for about 12 minutes by itself. Do not open the cap or bleeder screw during the cycle.
warnings: Primary is a BMW training document describing this routine for the N54 electric pump, which BMW says has the same coolant circuit as the N52; E90 N52 steps come from Pelican, two E90/E92 bimmerpost threads, an E60 N52 bleed PDF, z4-forum and the 2006 E60 PDF.
Keep the battery supply connected; do not open the cap while the pump is running.
The electric pump must not run dry (BMW training): fill the system before starting the routine.

steps.title: Top up after the cycle
steps.instruction: When the pump stops, open the cap slowly (it may hiss) and top up to the MAX mark (BMW training doc: check the level and top up to MAX if needed; Pelican and the 5series flush thread agree). Dissenting non-BMW values: 100 ml above MAX (E60 flush PDF), 250 ml above MAX = 18 mm (E60 bleed PDF), ball indicator about 6 mm above the top of the filler neck (E90/E92 bimmerpost). Do not exceed MAX; the final cold check in step 14 sets the correct level.
warnings: Overfilling can overflow and leave residue that looks like a leak (E60 bleed PDF).
Treat the above-MAX figures as unverified outliers; no BMW document supports them.
steps.dissent: 100 ml above MAX (S5_FLUSHPDF), 250 ml / 18 mm above MAX (S5_BLEED), ball indicator 6 mm above filler neck top (BP_BLEED).

steps.title: Warm up and check for leaks; repeat if needed
steps.instruction: Start the engine, idle until it reaches operating temperature (about 95 C per one poster) and inspect the drains, hoses and cap for leaks. To repeat the venting cycle, switch the ignition fully off and take the key out for about 3 minutes so the DME can power down, then run steps 11-12 again.
warnings: Never open the cap on a hot engine.

steps.title: Re-check the level cold and after driving
steps.instruction: After the car has cooled fully, open the cap (step 4 method) and check that the level is between the MIN and MAX marks on the filler neck; top up slowly to the correct mark if low. Re-check after the next drives; posters repeated the venting cycle two to three times until the level stayed stable.
warnings: A level that keeps dropping means air is still working out or there is a leak; have the cause fixed (owner manual).

steps.title: Close the cap, refit covers, dispose of coolant
steps.instruction: Close the cap until it clicks (aligning cap and tank marks where present). Refit the radiator cover and engine undertray. Take used coolant to a recycling point.
warnings: Coolant is toxic; keep from pets and children.

safety: Never open the expansion tank cap on a hot engine or while the electric pump is cycling (owner manual: wait until the engine cools; release pressure by turning the cap slightly first).
Coolant is toxic; keep from pets and children, clean spills, dispose per local rules.
Keep a stable battery supply connected during every 12 minute pump cycle; use the under-hood jump posts, not the trunk posts.
Support the vehicle on stands, ramps or a lift; never rely on a jack.
Radiator drain plugs are plastic; hand-tighten only.
The electric coolant pump must not run dry (BMW training document): fill the system before the venting routine and do not run it on an empty system.
Do not publish a total capacity figure or a coolant specification code as verified: no BMW document was found for them.
Use BMW blue coolant (or a product the owner manual path would accept via a BMW center); one bimmerpost thread cites a BMW bulletin about gel from mixing coolant types (unverified, secondary).
missingEvidence: BMW TIS/Bentley (or any BMW document) value for total cooling system capacity of the E90 328i N52 (manual vs automatic); the owner manual Capacities table has none.
A TIS/Bentley page specific to the E90 N52 venting routine (the BMW training document covers the N54 and states the circuit equals the N52; E60 PDFs add non-BMW above-MAX figures).
Undertray and radiator-cover fastener head sizes and count on the E90 (OE catalog gives fastener types only).
Torque (if any) for the plastic radiator drain plugs and the expansion tank vent screw.
BMW-stated coolant service interval (Turner suggests every two years; retailer only).
Expansion tank position in the engine bay (left/right) was not established by any fetched source.
Coolant spec code GS 94000 / N 600 69.0 now has two hosts (BimmerWorld; motordoctor.fr engine-level listing) but no BMW document and no E90-specific listing: stays VERIFIED_SECONDARY, not primary.
Which ZF/GM automatic (GA6L45R vs GA6HP19Z) is fitted; irrelevant to the coolant procedure and not resolvable from the VIN remotely.

visuals.title: Coolant expansion tank: filler cap, vent screw and level marks

elements.describe: The plastic coolant expansion tank with a screw-on filler cap and a filler neck carrying MIN and MAX level marks.
The screw cap on the expansion tank; turned slightly counter-clockwise first to release pressure, closed until it clicks.
A small M10 vent (bleeder) screw on the expansion tank, closed during venting and loosened only while filling.
MIN and MAX marks on the filler neck, plus a level indicator that one source calls a ball float.

facts.note: OE catalog lists expansion tank 17137640514; Pelican, bimmerpost and the owner manual describe filling and checking it.
Cap 17117639020, screw type; owner manual says turn slightly counter-clockwise to release pressure.
Release pressure by turning slightly counter-clockwise, then open; close until it clicks (owner manual).

OE catalog: vent screw M10 11537793373 on the expansion tank; Pelican: loosen the expansion tank bleeder screw while filling; bimmerpost: bleed screw on the coolant tank must be closed during venting.
Pelican: 'working at top of coolant expansion tank, loosen coolant expansion tank bleeder screw'; bimmerpost: 'that plastic screw on top of expansion tank' (bleed screw on the coolant tank).
youcanic (E90 article): tank is in the engine compartment in front of the passenger side; tpautorepair: on most E90 328i it is on the passenger side near the firewall.
Owner manual: MIN and MAX marks in the filler neck; E60 bleed PDF: MAX mark; bimmerpost: ball float indicator.
Exact mark shape and the ball float geometry are not described by any source. GAP.

The cap is on the expansion tank itself (owner manual: turn the expansion tank cap slightly counter-clockwise; Pelican: remove expansion tank cap), so it sits on the passenger-side tank; tpautorepair adds a black cap.

Which side of the engine bay it occupies is not established; draw it isolated, not placed in a specific corner.

visuals.title: Radiator drain plugs under the front of the car

A large plastic thumb-wheel drain plug at the bottom left of the radiator, turned by hand.
A second plastic drain plug at the bottom right of the radiator on some cars.
The fasteners and metal brackets that hold the radiator cover, removed so the plugs can be reached.

Plastic; a large thumb wheel turned by hand (5series flush thread); one source says red colour.

resolutionNotes: RESOLVED: coolant specification code. SINGLE_SOURCE -> VERIFIED_SECONDARY: BimmerWorld (GS 94000, N 600 690, G48) plus motordoctor.fr fitment listing for the N52B30A engine (BMW N 600 69.0, BMW GS 94000). Caveat: motordoctor lists X5 E70 with the same engine, and there is no BMW document. 'HT-12' is a Valvoline range name on that listing, not a BMW code, so the guide keeps 'genuine BMW blue coolant' as the buying instruction.

RESOLVED: transmission variant for this guide. VIN decode (guide 15) shows S205 automatic; catalog 3.73 final drive is tied to S205A. The automatic only changes the radiator/pipe part numbers and the capacity row; procedure unchanged. Treated as probable, not proven.
